convention.note: These four choices fully determine the byte<->Odu mapping. Changing any of them changes every byte value in the generated table. Do not change without bumping specVersion's major component.
convention.seniorityNote: Bascom's terminology. He examined 86 lists from 61 sources and found this order predominant (42 of 86, including 30 of 60 Yoruba lists, 5 of 6 Cuban, and the single Brazilian list). Twenty-one other rankings are recorded. Bascom 1969 pp. 47-48.

verification.summary: All 16 verified 2026-07-28 against Bascom (1969) Table 1 p. 4 and Table 3 column B p. 48, read via Internet Archive controlled lending. Every bit pattern and every seniority rank matched with no corrections needed.
acceptedSources: Bascom, William R. (1969) Ifa Divination, Indiana University Press
Abimbola, Wande (1976) Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus, Oxford University Press
Olagunju, James, Adeyefa & Joseph (2023) Algebraic characterization of Ifa main divination codes, Scientific African 20:e01729, doi:10.1016/j.sciaf.2023.e01729
structuralChecks: the 16 legs cover every 4-bit value exactly once
each consecutive seniority pair is a bitwise complement or reversal
verification.note: Structural checks are enforced by tests and catch transcription errors, but they cannot establish that the table matches tradition. Only a primary source can. Record each check with scripts/verify_odu.py.

corroboration.note: NOT verification. Recorded because it is independent visual evidence and because it bears directly on the one claim that disputed this table. Source quality is too low to change any figure's status: an anonymous YouTube Short showing a hand-drawn chart. It cannot be cited, and a practitioner's authority cannot be checked from a video.
corroboration.source: YouTube Short 'THE IMPRINTS OF THE SIXTEEN MAJOR ODU IFA, USING THE OPELE.', channel @charlesurubusi9492, https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Fq-wZvjXRdg
corroboration.convention: Open circle read as one mark (bit 1), filled circle as two marks (bit 0), top row most significant — the same convention this dataset uses.
corroboration.bearingOnDispute: Ọ̀sá read as 0111 and Òtúrúpọ̀n as 0010, matching this dataset. The untraceable search-engine claim had them swapped. That claim is now contradicted by the only real evidence found, but both remain unverified and should still be checked first against a citable source.

history.2026-07-28-web-attempt-failed: Open-web verification failed: the one peer-reviewed table was CAPTCHA-gated with no mirror. A search-engine summary asserted patterns for Ọ̀sá and Òtúrúpọ̀n conflicting with this table; the claim traced to no real page and was not acted on.
history.2026-07-28-video-corroboration: A hand-drawn chart in a YouTube Short agreed on 10 of 16. Recorded as corroboration only; not citable.
history.2026-07-28-resolved: Bascom Table 3B confirms Ọ̀sá = 0111 and Òtúrúpọ̀n = 0010. The search-engine claim was wrong. Declining to act on it was correct.

alternativeOrders.name: ife
alternativeOrders.label: Ifẹ
alternativeOrders.note: The order Bascom follows throughout his study, given by four Ifẹ diviners and confirmed by Wyndham (1921:66), Odumọlayọ (1951:13) and Clarke (1939:252). Associated with Ifẹ, Ilẹṣa, Ekiti and Igbomina in the northeast. Differs from the default only in the order of two pairs: positions 5-8 and 11-14.
